title: Adjustments 2: protective buys
summary: Capping the risk of a sold option with a bought one further out: spreads, iron condors, what they cost and when they are worth it.

questions.q: You sold the 900 put. Which buy protects it?
questions.why: A protective put has the same type and sits further out of the money: below the sold strike.

questions.q: Sold 900 put for ₹6, bought 850 put for ₹2, lot size 100. What is the most you can lose?
What does a protective buy usually do to margin?
options: Lowers it, because the worst case is capped
questions.why: With the loss capped, less margin is needed to cover the worst case.

questions.q: When is protection most worth its cost?
options: Around results, when a gap can jump past your stop
questions.why: A stop can't act inside a gap; a bought option can.

questions.q: Before Level 6, the builder lets you buy an option only if it:
options: Protects a sold leg of the same type, further out, with no more lots
questions.why: Buying on its own unlocks at Level 6; before that a buy must protect a sell.
